Alex W: Heads up — planning a rolling reboot window in az24 tonight 00:30–03:00 UTC. Targeting driver/kernel hotfix that fixes nvlink stalls seen in the last week.
Camila R: What's the plan for capacity? how many nodes per cohort?
Alex W: We'll do cohorts of 4 nodes per rack, sequentially. Pool 'saturn' will be drained 4 nodes at a time, backfill from spare pool 'saturn-standby' where possible. Estimated max capacity hit 6-10% during peak of the window.
Priya S: Any tenant prioritization? we should protect enterprise tenants with reserved capacity.
Alex W: Yes — enterprise reservations (tenants tagged enterprise:) will be pinned to warmback nodes. Non-reserved jobs may get preempted. We'll adjust autoscaler to favor reserved pools.
Mike L: Rollout steps + rollback?
Alex W: Runbook: 1) mark cohort for maintenance, 2) drain tasks, 3) node reboot, 4) kv-cache reseed on surviving nodes, 5) reopen. Rollback: abort before reboot or failover to standby if regressions.
ops-bot: automation note: executing preflight checks now: kernel version diff, active-job-count, egress-util. See link: https://confluence.redwood/az24-maint-preflight
Camila R: We should warm the KV cache before we open each cohort back to production. Cold-cache increases p99 by ~80ms, last time.
Priya S: Agree. Suggest sequence: drain -> reboot -> seed kv with top prefixes -> validate tail-latency -> open. Add a 10-min soak for canary.
Alex W: Good call. We'll do a 10-min canary per cohort (one node in cohort opened first). If p99 > baseline + 120ms we abort.
Mike L: Who's on-call for rollback?
sre-rotation: I'm on-call and monitoring from 00:15 UTC. Will escalate to Mike if we hit regression.
Camila R: Network side — we need to watch egress queue length during drain. Last time egress spikes caused throttling in az24. Ops-bot, can you emit expected egress baseline?
ops-bot: egress baseline (az24, pool saturn): 120-180MB/s last 24h. Expected bump during drain ~+15-30%. Alerts will trigger at 250MB/s.
Alex W: Cost note: if we rely on burst spare instances from cloud provider we'll pay ~0.12$/GPU-hour extra for 2h window. Estimate additional spend ~ $900. Ops: confirm budget ok.
Priya S: Approve given SLA windows, tag cost to project INFRA-MAINT.
Mike L: Quick check — are any customers running long-latency training jobs that will be affected?
Camila R: I've scanned job tags; two long jobs from team-research. I've messaged the owners to quiesce before 23:30 UTC.
Alex W: Commands we'll run (example):
```
./infra drain --pool=saturn --cohort=az24-rack-7 --count=4 --grace=300
./infra reboot --node-list=@cohort
./infra kv-seed --pool=saturn --prefixes=top100
```
Priya S: Add post-checks: synthetic-load p50/p95/p99 via perf-suite and compare to baseline. If p99 delta > 120ms revert.
ops-bot: scheduled job created: az24-maint-6598765432 with tags [maintenance, az24, saturn]. Preflight run completed OK.
Alex W: Timeline: 00:15 preflight + canary tests; 00:30 start cohort 1; repeating until ~03:00 finish. Will post progress updates in this thread.
Mike L: I can be awake for the first two cohorts. If anything weird, ping me.
Camila R: I'll monitor KV hit-rate dashboards and egress Qs.
Priya S: I'll validate latency regression tests and sign off per-cohort.
sre-rotation: Noted. Pager rules enabled for the window; escalation to infra-leads if any >5% error increase.
Alex W: Final ask — react with :thumbsup: if you ack and are available. I'll post a short status ping at cohort boundaries.
Camila R: :thumbsup:
Priya S: :thumbsup:
Mike L: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: preflight artifact attached: sha256:ab12... (logs stored in /var/maintenance/az24/6598765432)
Alex W: Thanks — starting monitoring.
ops-bot: NOTE: if nvlink error rate rises above 0.2% across cohort, automation will pause and notify #eng-infra-alerts.
